html:
Rila Monastery is the largest Orthodox monastery in Bulgaria, in the Rila Mountains south of Sofia, founded in the 900s by the hermit Ivan of Rila, the country's patron saint.

It was rebuilt in the 1300s by a local lord, whose tower still stands, and again in the 1830s and 1840s after a fire, with striped arches and painted galleries around a large courtyard. Under Ottoman rule it kept Bulgarian books, schools and church art alive and was a centre of the national revival. Its frescoes are by Zahari Zograf and others. It holds a famous wooden cross carved with over a hundred tiny scenes. It has been a World Heritage Site since 1983 and is a symbol of Bulgaria and of the Orthodox faith.
sum: Rila Monastery is the largest Orthodox monastery in Bulgaria, in the Rila Mountains south of Sofia, founded in the 900s by the hermit Ivan of Rila, the country's patron saint.
